title: Latency-aware KV precision gating and early dequant pipeline
creator: Ananya Patel
description: Objective: Reduce end-to-end decode latency for streaming/chunked workloads by avoiding unnecessary dequant work on KV cache and early tokens while preserving generation quality. Background: Dequantization of cached KV blocks and eager casting of whole attention windows is a measurable contributor to tail latency on INT8/FP8 mixed-precision paths, especially for short responses and high concurrency. We need a runtime strategy that gates precision conversion at token granularity, allows speculative/partial dequant for likely-needed prefix slices, and integrates with the prefill -> decode scheduler so that we overlap safe-precision work with GPU prefetching.
approach: Add a lightweight KV precision classifier that tags cached segments as 'hot' vs 'cold' based on recent reuse frequency, token entropy, and request SLA tier.
Implement token-granular gating: during decode, only dequantize KV shards that intersect the current attention window; leave remainder in packed int8/bit-packed FP8 until accessed.
Speculative early-dequant: when scheduler predicts imminent reuse (short horizon), issue a low-priority stream to dequant small prefix slices to hide latency behind current kernel execution.

Kernel selection heuristic: extend existing kernel scorer to include dequant overhead estimate and bandwidth pressure; prefer fused dequant+attn kernels when the amortized cost per token drops below threshold.
Scheduler integration: update prefill planner to order requests so that predictions for hot shards are staged earlier, enabling overlap with KV load and release of compute resources sooner.
Telemetry: emit per-token dequant latency, speculative hit rate, quality delta (BLEU/EM/LL) vs full-precision baseline, and failure/revert rate for gated tokens.
Safety: fall back to full eager dequant on SLO-violation paths and provide config knob per-customer (dedicated/private) to turn off gating.
Testing: synthetic microbench with short-response/long-context mixes, end-to-end A/B on hosted API with traffic split for latencies and quality regression monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: P0 workloads: 10-25% reduction in p95 token-latency for short (<128 token) responses on INT8 path without >0.5% quality regression.
Speculative early-dequant hit rate >= 70% on controlled workload; when hit, no increase in CPU overhead >5%.
No regression in throughput for high-concurrency mixed workloads (within 3% of baseline).
Feature gated behind runtime flag and customer config; telemetry surfaced in Console rollout dashboard.
PR with unit + integration tests, e2e perf benchmark reproducible in CI infra.
